trigger.request_payload: Review current official AI monitoring and observability trends, validate the need, then implement and release QIF v0.8.11 Late-Signal Reopen and Closure Calibration. Preserve the original incident closure as immutable history; distinguish event occurrence time from receipt time; require traceable late-signal source evidence, materiality assessment, accountable human reopen decisions, and closure calibration against later outcomes. Keep counts as evidence only. Do not claim source authenticity, causality, operational truth, autonomous authority, or semantic quality truth. Maintain at least three future roadmap horizons and use AOF v12.2.0 runtime evidence.

asked_questions: Which service touchpoint or environment should this redesign cover, and what should stay out of scope?
How should improvement success be judged: which metric or end state matters most?

user_answers.question: Which service touchpoint or environment should this redesign cover, and what should stay out of scope?
user_answers.answer: Cover the standalone calibration-report package, schema, deterministic verifier, example, retained negative fixtures, documentation, AI authoring guide, roadmap, portable package, AOF evidence, Git tag, and GitHub Release. Exclude UI, hosted monitoring integrations, raw sensitive telemetry, real incident operations, automatic reopening, employee surveillance, and claims of semantic or causal truth.

user_answers.question: How should improvement success be judged: which metric or end state matters most?
user_answers.answer: Success means a late signal records occurrence and receipt time, resolves to preserved source evidence and original closure, reproduces materiality and human reopen or keep-closed decisions without mutating history, calibrates the prior closure against later outcomes, routes uncertainty and conflict to governance, passes all QIF/AOF tests, and publishes the exact verified commit as v0.8.11.
